rules.name: Epistemic audit before valuation
rules.origin: Auditor operationalization of cited investor evidence; checklist and scenarios are not quotations or claimed historical procedures.
operational_steps: Separate known, unknown, irrelevant-to-thesis and potential unknown-unknown risks.
Write the strongest contrary explanation using its best evidence.
Reject a crucial assumption lacking a defensible evidence path rather than fill it with a sector stereotype.
rules.fits: Deeply understood businesses with honest uncertainty ranges
rules.does_not_fit: A fluent narrative masking an essential knowledge gap
rules.hard_numeric_threshold: Not established unless a cited claim explicitly supplies one.

entity_names.BYD_holder: Himalaya Capital Investors, L.P. (formerly LL Investment Partners, L.P.)

identity.roles: Founder and chairman of Himalaya; official biography states principal-fund management since 1997. The 2013 interview documents16years running Himalaya, independently consistent with that history.
identity.mandate_and_era: Early long/short activity was abandoned around 2004 according to the 2013 interview. Later business-owner framework should not be imputed unchanged to the 1997 start. Current official mandate has geographic/business focus, not a rule of buying every Chinese company.
identity.personal_vs_fund: Controlled corporate beneficial interests and adviser reports do not equal Li Lu’s wholly personal capital or every decision he made.

fit_and_no_fit.fit: Auditor interpretation: businesses allowing deep research into durable advantage, adaptive organization and trustworthy capital allocation. BYD demonstrates that significant technological change can fit when the specific competence and price argument are established.
